message.content:
In the memos repo at /bench/repo, answer with exact path:line citations:

1. Something in the server keeps links to externally-stored attachment content (e.g. S3 presigned URLs) from going stale. Find the component (likely under server/runner/), its schedule (interval constant), and where it is wired into server startup (which file/line calls/starts it, e.g. in server/server.go Start()). Give exact line numbers of: the runner type, the ticker/interval, and the startup wiring call.

2. Third-party identity providers: which package defines the provider abstraction (interface) and which concrete protocol implementation package ships (e.g. plugin/idp and plugin/idp/oauth2)? Cite the interface declaration path:line and the concrete implementation path:line.

3. Is there ANY cron scheduler or nightly database-cleanup job in the codebase? Search for "cron", "midnight", "cleanup", "vacuum", scheduled jobs. List anything found (e.g. runners with tickers and their intervals) or state confidently nothing exists. Report all runners under server/runner/ with their schedules and where they're started.

Report thoroughness: very thorough. Return concise findings with path:line for every claim.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Scheduler Plugin

A production-ready, GitHub Actions-inspired cron job scheduler for Go.

## Features

- **Standard Cron Syntax**: Supports both 5-field and 6-field (with seconds) cron expressions
- **Timezone-Aware**: Explicit timezone handling to avoid DST surprises
- **Middleware Pattern**: Composable job wrappers for logging, metrics, panic recovery, timeouts
- **Graceful Shutdown**: Jobs complete cleanly or cancel when context expires
- **Zero Dependencies**: Core functionality uses only the standard library
- **Type-Safe**: Strong typing with clear error messages
- **Well-Tested**: Comprehensive test coverage

## Installation

This package is included with Memos. No separate installation required.

Findings below. Two of your three premises need correction.

## 1. S3 presign refresh runner — confirmed

- **Runner type**: `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16` (`type Runner struct`), constructor at `:20`
- **Interval constant**: `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27` — `const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` (comment "Schedule runner every 12 hours" at `:26`)
- **Ticker**: `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:30` — `ticker := time.NewTicker(runnerInterval)`
- **Startup wiring**: `Start()` calls `s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)` at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:129`. Inside `startBackgroundRunners` (`/bench/repo/server/server.go:153`):
  - `/bench/repo/server/server.go:162` — `s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)`
  - `/bench/repo/server/server.go:163` — `s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)` (synchronous priming pass on boot)
  - `/bench/repo/server/server.go:169` — `s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)` in a goroutine
  - Import: `/bench/repo/server/server.go:25`
- Staleness rule: re-presigns only when the URL is within 1 day of expiry — `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:88` skips if `LastPresignedTime + 4*24h` is still in the future (URLs are issued with 5-day expiry).
- Shutdown: cancel funcs registered at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:159`, stopped at `:140`/`:176`, awaited at `:143`/`:184`.

## 2. Identity providers — **no interface exists**

Correction on both counts: the packages are `internal/idp` and `internal/idp/oauth2`, **not** `plugin/idp` (there is no `plugin/` directory at the repo root).

More importantly, **there is no provider abstraction interface**. `/bench/repo/internal/idp/idp.go` is 8 lines total and declares only a plain data struct:

```go
package idp

type IdentityProviderUserInfo struct {  // idp.go:3
	Identifier  string
	DisplayName string
	Email       string
	AvatarURL   string
}
```

`grep -rn "interface" internal/idp/` returns zero matches.

- **Concrete implementation**: `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:20` — `type IdentityProvider struct`, constructor `NewIdentityProvider` at `:27`. Methods: `ExchangeToken` at `:47`, `UserInfo` at `:83`. It is the only implementation shipped.
- Because there is no interface, dispatch is a hardcoded type check rather than polymorphism: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:120` — `if identityProvider.Type == storepb.IdentityProvider_OAUTH2 {`, then directly constructing `oauth2.NewIdentityProvider(...)` at `:121`. Adding a second protocol (OIDC/SAML/LDAP) would require editing this branch.

## 3. Cron / scheduled cleanup — a full cron package exists but is **completely unwired**

Correction: a cron scheduler *does* exist, but nothing in the server ever uses it.

`/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/` is a complete, tested cron implementation (12 files):
- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:12` — `type Scheduler struct`; `New` at `:54`
- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/parser.go:30` — `ParseCronExpression`, supports 5- and 6-field syntax
- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/job.go:19` — `Schedule` cron-expression field; validation at `:49`
- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/middleware.go`, `doc.go`, `README.md`

**It is dead code.** `grep -rn "internal/scheduler"` outside the package itself returns only its own two test files (`integration_test.go:13`, `example_test.go:10`). No production caller. Its README even calls it a "Scheduler Plugin," suggesting it was written against the missing `plugin/` layout.

The "midnight" hits are test fixtures only: `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/parser_test.go:17` and `job.go:21` (doc comment example `"0 0 * * *"`).

**No nightly database cleanup, no VACUUM, no retention/purge job exists anywhere.** `grep -rniE "vacuum"` across all Go files returns zero results.

### All runners under `server/runner/` (complete inventory — only 2)

| Runner | Schedule | Started at |
|---|---|---|
| `s3presign` — `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16` | 12h ticker (`:27`, `:30`) | `/bench/repo/server/server.go:162-169` |
| `memopayload` — `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:14` | **None** — no ticker, no interval; only `RunOnce` at `:27` | **Never started.** `NewRunner` (`:19`) has zero callers repo-wide |

Note on `memopayload`: despite living under `server/runner/`, its `Runner`/`NewRunner` are unreferenced. Only its free function `RebuildMemoPayload` is used, called inline from request handlers at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447`.

### Other periodic tickers outside `server/runner/`

- **Cache expiry sweep** (in-memory only, not DB): `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:201` ticker on `CleanupInterval`, default **5 minutes** (`:60`, with `DefaultTTL` 10m at `:59`). Goroutine launched from `New` at `:83`; three instances created at `/bench/repo/store/store.go:51-53`.
- **SSE heartbeat**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go:17` — `sseHeartbeatInterval = 30 * time.Second`, ticker at `:64`.
- `/bench/repo/store/test/containers.go:164` — 500ms poll, test helper only.
